HERSCHEL JUNIOR WALKER.background: Born March 3, 1962, in Augusta, Georgia; raised in Wrightsville, Georgia; Johnson County High School (1979 state champion). University of Georgia running back 1980-1982 (1980 national championship, 1982 Heisman Trophy); left early for the USFL (New Jersey Generals 1983-1985, 1985 league MVP), then NFL with Dallas, Minnesota, Philadelphia, the N.Y. HERSCHEL JUNIOR WALKER.ideology: His 2022 campaign site described him as 'a compassionate conservative who is pro-life and pro-family.' He entered the race with Donald Trump's endorsement and was also backed by Senate Minority Leader Mitch McConnell and a broad slate of GOP figures including Gov. Brian Kemp, per Wikipedia. Primary rival Gary Black and Lt. Gov. Geoff Duncan are listed as having declined to endorse him.
HERSCHEL JUNIOR WALKER.record: Not an officeholder before 2025 apart from chairing the President's Council on Sports, Fitness, and Nutrition (2018 appointment). Coverage of the campaign included the AJC's findings that his claims about his companies' size and his law-enforcement work were inflated or unverifiable; his residency in Texas (he registered to vote in Georgia in Aug. 2021 at a Buckhead home owned by his wife); reports in Oct. 2022 that he had paid for a 2009 abortion and a second woman's allegation he pressured her to have one in 1993, both of which he denied ('I never paid for an abortion'); and past police reports he has attributed to dissociative identity disorder, diagnosed in 2001 and described in his 2008 book Breaking Free. Wikipedia says he ran 203,130 votes behind Gov. Kemp in Nov. 2022. Since Dec. 2025 he has served as U.S. ambassador to the Bahamas.

TREA PIPKIN.background: John A. "Trea" Pipkin III, born and raised in Henry County; lives in McDonough with his wife. Associate's degree in business administration, Reinhardt College; bachelor's in risk management, University of Georgia; law degree, Georgia State University College of Law. While solicitor-general, served on the executive council of the Solicitors-General Association of Georgia and as vice-chair of the Prosecuting Attorneys' Council. Adjunct teaching in criminal law at Gordon State College, Mercer University and Emory University School of Law; boards of Haven House and Speedway Children's Charities; Reinhardt University trustee.
